applicableAreas: Construction near transmission poles and guy wires at NW and SW corners along Valley View Road
findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 3) states: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction. Call Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule a tailgate safety meeting.' This requirement is documented on the plans. However, no evidence exists that this meeting has been scheduled, completed, or documented. Sheet 4 existing conditions survey confirms two power poles with guy wires exist at NW and SW corners on Valley View Road frontage. Construction is proposed within or immediately adjacent to these facilities (excavation visible on Sheet 11 near NW pole). No certificate or documentation of completed pre-construction safety meeting is provided in the site plan submittal.
findings.reasoning: While the site plan acknowledges the pre-construction coordination requirement by referencing the Austin Energy contact and the 48-hour notice requirement, there is no affirmative evidence that this meeting has been scheduled or completed. This is a procedural requirement that must be satisfied before construction begins. The presence of the requirement on the plans is not equivalent to compliance; completion documentation is necessary to confirm the deficiency is resolved.
findings.comment: Pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy not documented as scheduled or completed. Site plan references Andrew Perez contact information but provides no evidence of meeting confirmation 48 hours before construction.

findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 13 (Fire Department requirements) and other construction notes reference standard disclaimers about utilities. Sheet 3 mentions 'Texas 811 Call Before You Dig' requirement in boilerplate but specific One Call (1-800-344-8377) contact notification is not explicitly documented in construction notes. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows excavation at NW corner with approximately 3-foot cuts proposed, but no specific construction note references One Call notification for underground electric facility verification.
findings.reasoning: While the Texas 811 logo appears on multiple sheets as a standard boilerplate element, the specific requirement to contact One Call (1-800-344-8377) before digging to locate and mark underground electric facilities is not explicitly stated in the construction notes reviewed. Given that Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing and Sheet 11 shows significant excavation/grading, specific One Call notification documentation is required but not provided in the plans.
findings.comment: One Call (1-800-344-8377) contact requirement not explicitly documented in construction notes despite significant excavation and underground electric service routing proposed.

applicableAreas: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly depicts a power pole (labeled 'P.P.') with guy wire (labeled 'GUY') at the NW corner of the property along Valley View Road. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows significant grading and excavation occurring immediately adjacent to and potentially within 25 feet of this transmission structure location. Specific contour analysis shows: existing grade at NW corner approximately 688-689 feet; proposed grade approximately 686.10-686.20 feet, indicating approximately 2-3 feet of excavation/cut occurring directly at the property line where the transmission pole is located. No notes on the grading plan indicate Austin Energy coordination, evaluation, or approval for this excavation.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 2) explicitly state: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors. Grading near electric transmission facilities must be coordinated with Austin Energy prior to commencement of grading.' The grading plan demonstrates that excavation is occurring at the exact location of the transmission structure (NW corner). No documentation of Austin Energy coordination or approval for this grading activity is visible on the plans. This constitutes a direct violation of the stated requirement.
findings.comment: Grading and excavation (approximately 3 feet of cut) proposed within 25 feet of transmission structure at NW corner without documented Austin Energy coordination or approval.

applicableAreas: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms transmission pole and guy anchor at NW corner. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) documents excavation depths showing proposed cut of approximately 2-3 feet at the NW corner property line where the transmission structure is located. This exceeds the 1-foot depth threshold that triggers the UCM § 1.14.5.2 evaluation requirement. No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that this excavation greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of the transmission foundation has been reviewed and approved is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.5.2 states that excavations greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of transmission foundations require Austin Energy evaluation and approval. The grading plan clearly shows excavation at the NW corner of approximately 2-3 feet in depth, which exceeds the 1-foot threshold. Without documentation of Austin Energy review and approval in the site plan submittal, this deficiency cannot be resolved. The presence of excavation specifications on the plan without the corresponding approval documentation demonstrates non-compliance.
findings.comment: Excavation exceeding 1 foot in depth (approximately 2-3 feet) within 25 feet of transmission structure lacks Austin Energy evaluation and approval documentation.

applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries where electric easements are located; landscape planting zones
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts numerous trees within and immediately adjacent to the 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries. Trees are coded as 'SY' (Street Yard), 'PL' (Parking Lot), 'P' (Buffer Point), and 'M' (Mitigation) within or overlapping the utility line corridors. Sheet 31 guidance note states: 'Specific irrigation layout is not shown. The drawing does not visually map out sprinkler heads, lateral lines, or valves. Therefore, it cannot be visually confirmed if heads are placed within 25 feet of structures or easements. However...Given that plantings (which require water) are shown in these areas, it is highly likely irrigation infrastructure will be present near the utilities.' Sheet 31 (Irrigation Notes) defers specific irrigation system design to an as-built plan: 'THE IRRIGATION INSTALLER SHALL DEVELOP AND PROVIDE AN AS-BUILT DESIGN PLAN TO THE CITY.' No specific irrigation layout showing sprinkler clearances from transmission structures is provided on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 14) state: 'Sprinklers are prohibited within 25 feet of transmission poles and structures.' Sheet 31 shows that significant plantings requiring irrigation are located within and immediately adjacent to transmission easements. The specific irrigation system layout, including sprinkler head locations and distances from transmission structures, is deferred to an as-built plan not included in this submittal. While it may be possible that the final irrigation design will comply with clearance requirements, the current plans do not affirmatively demonstrate compliance with the 25-foot prohibition. Approval cannot be granted without documentation showing that irrigation infrastructure will maintain required clearances.
findings.comment: Irrigation system layout deferred to as-built plan; specific sprinkler clearances from transmission structures within 25 feet not documented despite plantings shown within easement areas requiring irrigation.

applicableAreas: Northeast corner of site, biofiltration/detention pond area adjacent to transmission easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a 'Biofiltration/Detention Pond' located in the northeast corner of the site, immediately adjacent to the north property line where a 5-foot electric easement and a 15-foot drainage easement/electric easement are located. Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan) and Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) detail the pond design and dimensions. The pond perimeter and retaining wall are shown immediately adjacent to the property boundary where the transmission easement is located. The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 16) explicitly prohibit: 'any structures, including but not limited to...drainage, filtration or detention ponds which would impair Austin Energy's access to the transmission easements or its lines, poles, structures, towers or appurtenant facilities in the easements.' The site plan does not provide documentation that the pond design has been reviewed for impact on transmission facility access or that the pond can be maintained while preserving Austin Energy's turnaround and maintenance vehicle access requirements.
findings.reasoning: While water quality features (detention ponds) may be allowable outside transmission easements with appropriate setbacks, the proposed pond's immediate adjacency to the transmission easement boundary raises questions about whether it impairs Austin Energy access as prohibited. The Electric Transmission Notes require that features not impair access, and the transmission facility access requirements (including 25-foot clearance from structure base for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles) must be verified. The site plan does not contain documentation that Austin Energy has reviewed and approved the pond location relative to access and maintenance requirements. The proximity of the pond with retaining wall immediately at the easement boundary creates uncertainty about whether the design preserves required access.
findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond with retaining wall proposed immediately adjacent to northeast corner transmission easement; no documentation that pond design preserves Austin Energy access and maintenance vehicle turnaround requirements.

applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries within and adjacent to electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts multiple trees and shrubs (coded as 'SY', 'PL', 'P', 'M') positioned directly on or overlapping the 5-foot electric easement boundaries along the north, east, and south property lines. Specific vision analysis identified: 'North Boundary: Numerous large tree canopies (indicated by circles) are drawn directly on or overlapping this line and the property boundary'; 'South Boundary: Large tree canopies are drawn overlapping this area'; 'East Boundary: Tree canopies overlap the property line in this area.' These planted trees and associated shrubs will mature and create dense vegetation directly within and immediately adjacent to the transmission easements. Sheet 31 does not provide density, spacing, or height specifications that would allow verification that plantings will not obstruct access to structure bases during maintenance.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 1) explicitly state: 'Vehicular access for Austin Energy trucks and equipment is always to be maintained within the easement' and 'Shrubbery must not obstruct access to structure base' (UCM § 1.14.6). Sheet 31 shows plantings directly on/within the easement boundaries. These plantings, as they mature, will create obstacles to the 'walking or vehicle access to transmission structure base' that must remain clear per the grouping's regulatory overview. Mature tree canopies and shrub plantings within the easement violate this requirement.
findings.comment: Shrubs and tree plantings with mature canopies proposed directly within and overlapping 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries; will obstruct required access to transmission structure base during maintenance.

applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries; northwest and southwest corners where transmission structures located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) show retaining walls proposed immediately along the north, east, and south property boundaries where the 5-foot electric easements are located. Specific observations: North boundary retaining wall immediately adjacent to north easement; East boundary: 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced' and new concrete fence at east property line within/adjacent to easement; South boundary: concrete retaining wall running 'tightly along the southern property line, parallel and immediately adjacent to the southern OHE line and 5' Electric & Tele Easement.' The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20) specify a '25-foot access corridor' that must remain 'level' and free for Austin Energy maintenance vehicles. The site plan shows retaining walls and permanent features immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries, eliminating any clear 25-foot access corridor for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles (Condor trucks) with 75-foot turning radius.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 requires a '25-foot access corridor' along the entire length of transmission ROW, with 'Level access...designed to support 46,000-48,000 lb tandem axle loads' for Condor truck turnaround. The site plan's placement of retaining walls and permanent structures immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries prevents the maintenance of this required corridor. The transmission facility access requirement (Condor truck turnaround with 75-foot turning radius) cannot be satisfied if permanent walls and features occupy the easement at property boundaries.
findings.comment: Retaining walls and permanent site features (concrete fence, pond perimeter wall) proposed immediately at/within transmission easement boundaries along north, east, and south property lines; prevents required 25-foot level access corridor for maintenance vehicle turnaround.

applicableAreas: NW and SW corners of property along Valley View Road where transmission structures and guy anchors located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows power poles ('P.P.') with guy wires ('GUY') and guy anchors at both the NW and SW corners of the property on Valley View Road. However, Sheets 9 (Site Plan) and 11 (Grading Plan) do not adequately depict these guy wire structures or establish 25-foot evaluation zones around them. The transmission notes require that guy anchors be treated as transmission structures for clearance purposes ('Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors'). While the poles themselves may be outside property boundaries, the guy anchors extend onto or very near the property, yet the grading plan shows excavation occurring at the NW corner with no indication of the guy anchor location or the required clearance envelope. The plans fail to show: (1) guy wire and anchor locations on grading and site plans, (2) 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors, and (3) how proposed site improvements (excavation, retaining walls) maintain clearance from guy anchors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Existing guy wire foundations and anchors' be 'shown on plans' and that 'proposed construction does not maintain required clearances from these support structures.' The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows guy wires and anchors exist at NW and SW corners. The grading and site plans do not adequately depict these structures or the 25-foot clearance zones required around them. The lack of guy anchor depiction on the working plans (Sheets 9 and 11) combined with proposed excavation at the NW corner creates uncertainty about whether clearances are maintained. Adequate depiction of guy anchors and clearance zones on all relevant working plans is required.
findings.comment: Guy wire anchor locations from existing conditions survey not adequately depicted on grading and site plans; 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors not established on working drawings despite proposed excavation at NW corner.

applicableAreas: Multiple locations: NW/SW corners (transmission poles), northeast corner (detention pond), north/east/south property lines (easements)
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing transmission poles and guy wires along Valley View Road (NW/SW corners) and multiple electric easements (5-foot and 15-foot) along property boundaries. Sheets 9, 11, and 15 show proposed improvements including: excavation at NW corner within/adjacent to transmission structure location; retaining walls along north, east, and south property lines within/adjacent to electric easements; biofiltration/detention pond in NE corner adjacent to transmission easement; landscape plantings within easement boundaries. The site plan indicates that electric easements exist but does not include documentation showing: (1) that Austin Energy has reviewed and approved proposed improvements relative to the easement; (2) how the site improvements will be modified/designed to avoid conflicts with transmission facility requirements; or (3) what tie-down arrangements or easement modifications (if any) have been agreed with Austin Energy. Site plan notes reference Austin Energy coordination requirements but do not document that the coordination has occurred or that conflicts have been resolved.
findings.reasoning: Proposed improvements (excavation, walls, pond, landscaping) occur within or immediately adjacent to existing transmission easements, but no documentation of Austin Energy review, approval, or conflict resolution is provided on the site plan. Documentation of easement coordination or relocation is needed.
findings.comment: Multiple proposed improvements (excavation, retaining walls, detention pond, landscaping) located within or immediately adjacent to existing electric easements without documented Austin Energy coordination, approval, or conflict resolution.
